## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Wide constrained beam search for generative retrieval materializes large vocabulary logits and repeatedly reads the same prompt KV for every beam. Add model-native trie constraints, compact semantic-ID (SID) output projection, and optional shared-context attention, with beam width selected independently for each request.

The implementation is based directly on upstream `main`, without release-branch backports or unrelated input-handling changes.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Discover and validate an optional model-bundled `trie_output_head.safetensors` artifact containing a three-codebook SID trie. Support dense or sparse valid-child masks, on-device prefix state, and constrained joint beam selection.
- Project active SID codebooks instead of materializing full-vocabulary decode logits on compatible CUDA/TP=1, unquantized, non-LoRA configurations. Preserve full-vocabulary normalization by default; `SGLANG_OPT_BEAM_TRIE_TOPK_LOGPROB=true` explicitly opts into approximate candidate-only normalization, which can change rankings.
- Add opt-in `SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_ATTENTION=true` for FlashInfer MHA with FP16/BF16 KV. Bucket groups by their request-specific widths and share prompt attention work while retaining per-beam decode suffixes. Unsupported backend/cache configurations use standard attention; attention logit caps are rejected on the shared-context path.
- Account for beam decode headroom at admission and retain histories on-device for fixed-length SID decoding. Separate native trie CUDA-graph variants from ordinary captures and replay trie/shared-context graphs with freshly staged metadata.
- Preserve speculative CUDA-graph runner compatibility with an inherited non-trie capture default and beam-only preparation keywords only for actual trie captures.
- Add CPU and CUDA-registered correctness tests, with documentation for the artifact schema, supported configurations, approximation semantics, and per-request beam widths in `python/sglang/srt/beam_search/README.md`. Benchmark and profiling utilities, model bundles, prompt corpora, valid-SID indexes, raw results, and profiles are outside this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on one NVIDIA H200 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Transformers 5.19.0, and tokenizers 0.23.2.

- Retained coverage: **141 tests and 82 subtests passed**, including core beam search, output-head behavior, scheduler/admission checks, upstream graph-runner tests, and four real CUDA attention/projection cases.
- End-to-end native decoding: four measured prompts each at beam widths 1,800 and 2,000 matched the previous revision's ordered SID outputs exactly. Every response had the requested count and no invalid or duplicate SIDs. Both cases replayed the shared-context trie graphs, without ordinary-graph fallback.

The retained suite was run from the repository root:

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/beam_search \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate.py \
  test/registered/unit/batch_overlap/test_tbo_filter_batch_marker.py \
  test/registered/unit/server_args/test_model_source_paths.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_beam_shared_context.py \

nodes.body:
Pushed fixes for:

- **KV reservation on every beam request**: only fixed-length trie groups now report an exact decode budget (`BeamGroup.decode_slot_budget()`), and the existing admission estimates use it without extra state; ordinary beam search keeps main's estimate. Priority preemption still skips beam groups, since `release_req` does not free a group's member rows (9934b0fe90).
- **FlashInfer hook on every decode layer**: shared-context attention is now `BeamSharedContextFlashInferAttnBackend`, a FlashInfer subclass selected only when `SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_ATTENTION` is set; `flashinfer_backend.py` is back to main. The workspace resize is dropped, since it only served 20k-row trie decode graphs (59fe6636e6).
- **Beam branches inside `_get_logits`**: `_get_logits` is back to main; `forward()` calls `_get_beam_trie_logits` for compact-trie rows (22f3d4b7cb).
- **Trie decode graph variant**: trie and shared-context batches run eagerly, which removes the capture kwargs shim and the extra `ShapeKey` field (0e91bff157).
- **Hub lookup on every model start**: the trie head loads only when `config.json` sets `"beam_trie_output_head": true`, through `cached_file`; a declared but missing artifact now fails startup instead of silently dropping the constraint (2e20e9605a).
- `BeamCoordinator` loads the trie itself, so `scheduler.py` is back to main (455831aa74).
- The trie and shared-context forward-batch fields are built in the beam modules; `ForwardBatch.init_new` makes two calls (6a3b3886bf).
- The Triton kernels move to `sglang.kernels.ops` (`attention.beam_shared_context`, `gemm.codebook_projection`, `grammar.trie_mask`) with their tests (881da8d2a5).

Verified on one H200 with a synthetic Qwen3-0.6B + 3x8192 SID model and a 1M-item trie, beam width 1000 and 2000: ordered beams match the previous head at concurrency 1 in eager, graph, shared-context, and mixed-width runs; the differences at concurrency 4-10 are within the previous head's own run-to-run variance; ordinary beam search matches main. Throughput is equal or higher, and peak memory is about 20 GB lower in graph mode.

Model bundles need `"beam_trie_output_head": true` in `config.json`.

### Full original LiHA: +7.2% completed QPS versus the previous PR head

Baseline is this OSS PR's previous head, `b2d120e596d1226012ba29daa6f588038e26ad07`. The update is `45b352b`; its final Git tree is identical to the measured implementation, before splitting that implementation into seven feature-sized commits.

Original full trie and unchanged model weights, with full-vocabulary projection/normalization. One H200, BF16 weights/KV, beam width 1,000, 1,000 three-token SIDs per request, and prefix cache disabled. Two fresh-process runs per version, each with 50 warmups and 1,000 measured requests. Offered load was 54 QPS using Poisson arrivals with no client-concurrency limit. Latency includes queueing through the complete response.

| Implementation | Mean completed QPS | Completed QPS, run 1 / 2 | p95 latency, run 1 / 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous PR head `b2d120e` | 49.70 | 49.756 / 49.635 | 2.059 / 2.514 s |
| This update `45b352b` | **53.28** | **52.776 / 53.789** | **0.976 / 1.272 s** |

All 4,000 measured responses had the requested count and length, with no invalid or duplicate SIDs. The controlled 1,000-request full-trie correctness replay produced **1,000/1,000 identical ordered SID lists**, **maximum sequence-score difference 0**, **mean/minimum Jaccard 1.0**, and **mean/minimum beam overlap 1,000/1,000**. Ordinary greedy output checks and mixed ordinary/beam compatibility probes passed. Controlled equality does not imply bitwise equality across arbitrary asynchronous batch geometries.

Runtime used the v0.5.21 dependency line: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18, SGLang kernel 0.4.7.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, Tokenizers 0.22.2, and CUDA Tile 1.6.0rc5. The current head's newer minimum-version startup guard was explicitly disabled for this compatibility run; dependency declarations were unchanged. Both versions used an isolated `beam_trie_output_head=true` config, unchanged weights/trie bytes, 32,032 sequence rows, memory fraction 0.30, MessagePack IPC, post-warmup GC freeze, configured GC thresholds, and delayed sampling disabled.

The baseline implementation always runs beam batches eagerly; its unused dense-graph capture capacity was reduced to 1,000 rows to avoid startup OOM without changing that serving path. This update captured exact 1,000-32,000-row trie graph buckets. These are measurements at the stated offered load, not estimates of globally maximal throughput. All earlier runs, including the earlier tail-latency outlier, were retained; this table reports the complete fresh rerun rather than selecting individual repetitions.

+"""Native Triton shared-context attention for wide beam decoding."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _shared_context_attention_kernel(
+    q,
+    k_buffer,
+    v_buffer,
+    row_indices,
+    context_slots,
+    context_cu_seqlens,
+    decode_slots,
+    decode_lens,
+    output,
+    softmax_scale,
+    stride_q_row,
+    stride_q_head,
+    stride_q_dim,
+    stride_row_group,
+    stride_row_beam,
+    stride_k_slot,
+    stride_k_head,
+    stride_k_dim,
+    stride_v_slot,
+    stride_v_head,
+    stride_v_dim,
+    stride_decode_group,
+    stride_decode_token,
+    stride_out_row,
+    stride_out_head,
+    stride_out_dim,
+    BEAM_WIDTH: tl.constexpr,
+    Q_PER_KV: tl.constexpr,
+    HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    MAX_DECODE: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    group = tl.program_id(0)
+    q_head = tl.program_id(1)
+    beam_block = tl.program_id(2)
+    kv_head = q_head // Q_PER_KV
+
+    beam_offsets = beam_block * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
+    context_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    dim_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)
+    beam_mask = beam_offsets < BEAM_WIDTH
+    dim_mask = dim_offsets < HEAD_DIM
+
+    rows = tl.load(
+        row_indices + group * stride_row_group + beam_offsets * stride_row_beam,
+        mask=beam_mask,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    q_offsets = (
+        rows[:, None] * stride_q_row
+        + q_head * stride_q_head
+        + dim_offsets[None, :] * stride_q_dim
+    )
+    q_values = tl.load(
+        q + q_offsets,
+        mask=beam_mask[:, None] & dim_mask[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    )
+
+    negative_infinity = -float("inf")
+    max_values = tl.where(beam_mask, negative_infinity, 0.0)
+    normalizers = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    accumulator = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_D), dtype=tl.float32)
+    softmax_scale_log2 = softmax_scale * 1.4426950408889634
+
+    context_start = tl.load(context_cu_seqlens + group)
+    context_end = tl.load(context_cu_seqlens + group + 1)
+    context_length = context_end - context_start
+
+    for block_start in tl.range(0, context_length, BLOCK_N):
+        token_offsets = block_start + context_offsets
+        token_mask = token_offsets < context_length
+        slots = tl.load(
+            context_slots + context_start + token_offsets,
+            mask=token_mask,
+            other=0,
+        )
+        k_offsets = (
+            slots[:, None] * stride_k_slot
+            + kv_head * stride_k_head
+            + dim_offsets[None, :] * stride_k_dim
+        )
+        v_offsets = (
+            slots[:, None] * stride_v_slot
+            + kv_head * stride_v_head
+            + dim_offsets[None, :] * stride_v_dim
+        )
+        k_values = tl.load(
+            k_buffer + k_offsets,
+            mask=token_mask[:, None] & dim_mask[None, :],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        v_values = tl.load(
+            v_buffer + v_offsets,
+            mask=token_mask[:, None] & dim_mask[None, :],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+
+        scores = tl.dot(q_values, tl.trans(k_values))
+        scores = tl.where(
+            beam_mask[:, None] & token_mask[None, :],
+            scores,
+            negative_infinity,
+        )
+        block_max = tl.max(scores, axis=1)
+        new_max = tl.maximum(max_values, block_max)
+        previous_scale = tl.exp2((max_values - new_max) * softmax_scale_log2)
+        probabilities = tl.exp2((scores - new_max[:, None]) * softmax_scale_log2)

+        accumulator = accumulator * previous_scale[:, None] + tl.dot(
+            probabilities.to(v_values.dtype),
+            v_values,
+        )
+        max_values = new_max
+

+    for step in range(0, MAX_DECODE):
+        step_valid = step < decode_length
+        decode_offsets = (
+            group * stride_decode_group
+            + (step * BEAM_WIDTH + beam_offsets) * stride_decode_token
+        )
+        slots = tl.load(
+            decode_slots + decode_offsets,
+            mask=beam_mask & step_valid,
+            other=0,
+        )
+        k_offsets = (
+            slots[:, None] * stride_k_slot
+            + kv_head * stride_k_head
+            + dim_offsets[None, :] * stride_k_dim
+        )
+        v_offsets = (
+            slots[:, None] * stride_v_slot
+            + kv_head * stride_v_head
+            + dim_offsets[None, :] * stride_v_dim
+        )
+        k_values = tl.load(
+            k_buffer + k_offsets,
+            mask=beam_mask[:, None] & step_valid & dim_mask[None, :],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        v_values = tl.load(
+            v_buffer + v_offsets,
+            mask=beam_mask[:, None] & step_valid & dim_mask[None, :],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        score_matrix = tl.dot(q_values, tl.trans(k_values))
+        diagonal_mask = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)[:, None] == tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)[None, :]
+        scores = tl.sum(
+            tl.where(diagonal_mask, score_matrix, 0.0),
+            axis=1,
+        )

+
+        new_max = tl.maximum(max_values, scores)
+        previous_scale = tl.exp2((max_values - new_max) * softmax_scale_log2)
+        current_scale = tl.exp2((scores - new_max) * softmax_scale_log2)
+        normalizers = normalizers * previous_scale + current_scale
+        accumulator = (
+            accumulator * previous_scale[:, None] + v_values * current_scale[:, None]
+        )
+        max_values = new_max
+
+    result = accumulator / normalizers[:, None]
+    output_offsets = (
+        rows[:, None] * stride_out_row
+        + q_head * stride_out_head
+        + dim_offsets[None, :] * stride_out_dim
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        output + output_offsets,
+        result,
+        mask=beam_mask[:, None] & dim_mask[None, :],
+    )
+
+
+def shared_context_attention(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    v_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    context_slots: torch.Tensor,
+    context_cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+    decode_slots: torch.Tensor,
+    decode_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    output: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    softmax_scale: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Apply shared prompt and per-beam suffix attention in one Triton kernel."""
+    if q.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError(f"Expected Q with 3 dimensions, got {q.shape}")
+    if k_buffer.ndim != 3 or v_buffer.shape != k_buffer.shape:
+        raise ValueError("K/V buffers must have matching [slots, heads, dim] shapes")
+
+    if row_indices.ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError("Row indices must have shape [groups, beam_width]")
+    num_groups, beam_width = row_indices.shape
+    _, q_heads, head_dim = q.shape
+    kv_heads = k_buffer.shape[1]
+    if q_heads % kv_heads:
+        raise ValueError(f"Q heads {q_heads} must be divisible by KV heads {kv_heads}")
+    if decode_slots.shape[0] != num_groups:
+        raise ValueError("Decode slot groups must match grouped Q")
+    if decode_slots.shape[1] % beam_width:
+        raise ValueError("Decode slot capacity must be divisible by beam width")
+    if decode_lens.shape != (num_groups,):
+        raise ValueError("Decode lengths must contain one value per beam group")
+    if context_cu_seqlens.shape != (num_groups + 1,):
+        raise ValueError("Context offsets must contain one boundary per beam group")
+    if output is None:
+        output = torch.empty_like(q)
+    elif output.shape != q.shape:
+        raise ValueError("Output must match Q shape")
+
+    high_group_count = num_groups >= 6
+    block_m = 64 if high_group_count else 128
+    block_n = 64 if high_group_count else 128
+    num_warps = 4 if high_group_count else 8
+    num_stages = 4 if high_group_count else 3
+
+    block_d = triton.next_power_of_2(head_dim)
+    grid = (
+        num_groups,
+        q_heads,
+        triton.cdiv(beam_width, block_m),
+    )
+    _shared_context_attention_kernel[grid](
+        q,
+        k_buffer,
+        v_buffer,
+        row_indices,
+        context_slots,
+        context_cu_seqlens,
+        decode_slots,
+        decode_lens,
+        output,
+        softmax_scale,
+        q.stride(0),
+        q.stride(1),
+        q.stride(2),
+        row_indices.stride(0),
+        row_indices.stride(1),
+        k_buffer.stride(0),
+        k_buffer.stride(1),
+        k_buffer.stride(2),
+        v_buffer.stride(0),
+        v_buffer.stride(1),
+        v_buffer.stride(2),
+        decode_slots.stride(0),
+        decode_slots.stride(1),
+        output.stride(0),
+        output.stride(1),
+        output.stride(2),
+        BEAM_WIDTH=beam_width,
+        Q_PER_KV=q_heads // kv_heads,
+        HEAD_DIM=head_dim,
+        MAX_DECODE=decode_slots.shape[1] // beam_width,
+        BLOCK_M=block_m,
+        BLOCK_N=block_n,
+        BLOCK_D=block_d,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+        num_stages=num_stages,
+    )
+    return output

+    depths,
+    permutation,
+    inverse_permutation,
+    group_offsets,
+    num_rows,

+    rank_2 = tl.cumsum(is_depth_2.to(tl.int32)) - 1
+    destinations = tl.where(
+        is_depth_0,
+        rank_0,
+        tl.where(is_depth_1, count_0 + rank_1, count_0 + count_1 + rank_2),
+    )
+    tl.store(permutation + destinations, rows, mask=valid)
+    tl.store(inverse_permutation + rows, destinations, mask=valid)
+    tl.store(group_offsets, count_0)
+    tl.store(group_offsets + 1, count_0 + count_1)
+    tl.store(group_offsets + 2, count_0 + count_1 + count_2)

+@triton.jit
+def _depth_block_counts_kernel(
+    depths,
+    block_counts,
+    num_rows,
+    block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    block = tl.program_id(0)
+    rows = block * block_size + tl.arange(0, block_size)
+    valid = rows < num_rows
+    row_depths = tl.load(depths + rows, mask=valid, other=-1)
+    tl.store(
+        block_counts + block * 3,
+        tl.sum((valid & (row_depths <= 0)).to(tl.int32)),
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        block_counts + block * 3 + 1,
+        tl.sum((row_depths == 1).to(tl.int32)),
+    )
+    tl.store(

+

+@triton.jit
+def _depth_block_offsets_kernel(
+    block_counts,
+    block_offsets,
+    group_offsets,
+    num_blocks,
+    block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    blocks = tl.arange(0, block_size)
+    valid = blocks < num_blocks
+    counts_0 = tl.load(block_counts + blocks * 3, mask=valid, other=0)
+    counts_1 = tl.load(block_counts + blocks * 3 + 1, mask=valid, other=0)
+    counts_2 = tl.load(block_counts + blocks * 3 + 2, mask=valid, other=0)
+    total_0 = tl.sum(counts_0)
+    total_1 = tl.sum(counts_1)
+    total_2 = tl.sum(counts_2)
+    tl.store(
+        block_offsets + blocks * 3,
+        tl.cumsum(counts_0) - counts_0,
+        mask=valid,
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        block_offsets + blocks * 3 + 1,
+        total_0 + tl.cumsum(counts_1) - counts_1,
+        mask=valid,
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        block_offsets + blocks * 3 + 2,
+        total_0 + total_1 + tl.cumsum(counts_2) - counts_2,
+        mask=valid,
+    )
+    tl.store(group_offsets, total_0)
+    tl.store(group_offsets + 1, total_0 + total_1)
+    tl.store(group_offsets + 2, total_0 + total_1 + total_2)

+def _stable_depth_scatter_kernel(
+    depths,
+    block_offsets,

+    block = tl.program_id(0)
+    rows = block * block_size + tl.arange(0, block_size)
+    valid = rows < num_rows

+    is_depth_0 = valid & (row_depths <= 0)
+    is_depth_1 = valid & (row_depths == 1)
+    is_depth_2 = valid & (row_depths >= 2)
+    rank_0 = tl.cumsum(is_depth_0.to(tl.int32)) - 1
+    rank_1 = tl.cumsum(is_depth_1.to(tl.int32)) - 1
+    rank_2 = tl.cumsum(is_depth_2.to(tl.int32)) - 1
+    base_0 = tl.load(block_offsets + block * 3)
+    base_1 = tl.load(block_offsets + block * 3 + 1)
+    base_2 = tl.load(block_offsets + block * 3 + 2)
+    destinations = tl.where(
+        is_depth_0,
+        base_0 + rank_0,
+        tl.where(is_depth_1, base_1 + rank_1, base_2 + rank_2),
+    )
+    tl.store(permutation + destinations, rows, mask=valid)
+    tl.store(inverse_permutation + rows, destinations, mask=valid)
+

+def _stable_depth_partition(
+    depths: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    num_rows = depths.shape[0]

+    inverse_permutation = torch.empty_like(permutation)
+    group_offsets = torch.empty(3, dtype=torch.int32, device=depths.device)
+    if num_rows <= _SINGLE_BLOCK_PARTITION_MAX_ROWS:
+        _stable_depth_partition_kernel[(1,)](
+            depths,
+            permutation,
+            inverse_permutation,
+            group_offsets,
+            num_rows,
+            block_size=triton.next_power_of_2(num_rows),
+            num_warps=8,
+        )
+        return permutation, inverse_permutation, group_offsets
+
+    num_blocks = triton.cdiv(num_rows, _PARTITION_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    block_counts = torch.empty((num_blocks, 3), dtype=torch.int32, device=depths.device)
+    block_offsets = torch.empty_like(block_counts)
+    _depth_block_counts_kernel[(num_blocks,)](
+        depths,
+        block_counts,
+        num_rows,
+        block_size=_PARTITION_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    _depth_block_offsets_kernel[(1,)](
+        block_counts,
+        block_offsets,
+        group_offsets,
+        num_blocks,
+        block_size=triton.next_power_of_2(num_blocks),
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    _stable_depth_scatter_kernel[(num_blocks,)](
+        depths,
+        block_offsets,
+        permutation,
+        inverse_permutation,
+        num_rows,
+        block_size=_PARTITION_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return permutation, inverse_permutation, group_offsets
+
+
+def _supports_grouped_projection(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    codebook_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    depths: torch.Tensor,

+        and torch.version.cuda is not None
+        and hidden_states.is_cuda
+        and hidden_states.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and codebook_weights.dtype == torch.bfloat16

+

+def project_active_codebook_logits(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    codebook_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    depths: torch.Tensor,

+) -> torch.Tensor | None:

+        num_codebooks != _GROUPED_PROJECTION_CODEBOOKS

+            hidden_states,
+            codebook_weights,
+            depths,

+    ):

+
+    permutation, inverse_permutation, group_offsets = _stable_depth_partition(depths)
+

+        num_codebooks,
+        codebook_size,
+        hidden_size,
+    ).transpose(1, 2)
+    sorted_logits = torch._grouped_mm(
+        hidden_states[permutation],
+        grouped_weights,
+        group_offsets,
+    )
+    return sorted_logits[inverse_permutation]

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _materialize_mask_kernel(
+    pair_rows,
+    offsets,
+    values,
+    output,
+    output_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    pair = tl.load(pair_rows + row).to(tl.int64)
+    start = tl.load(offsets + pair).to(tl.int64)
+    end = tl.load(offsets + pair + 1).to(tl.int64)
+    positions = tl.arange(0, block_size)
+    valid = positions < end - start
+    children = tl.load(
+        values + start + positions,
+        mask=valid,
+        other=0,
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    tl.store(
+        output + row * output_row_stride + children,
+        1,
+        mask=valid,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _mask_logits_kernel(
+    logits,
+    pair_rows,
+    offsets,
+    values,
+    output,
+    logits_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    output_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    pair = tl.load(pair_rows + row).to(tl.int64)
+    start = tl.load(offsets + pair).to(tl.int64)
+    end = tl.load(offsets + pair + 1).to(tl.int64)
+    positions = tl.arange(0, block_size)
+    valid = positions < end - start
+    children = tl.load(
+        values + start + positions,
+        mask=valid,
+        other=0,
+    ).to(tl.int64)
+    scores = tl.load(
+        logits + row * logits_row_stride + children,
+        mask=valid,
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        output + row * output_row_stride + children,
+        scores,
+        mask=valid,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _mask_sparse_prefix_logits_kernel(
+    logits,
+    prefixes,
+    keys,
+    offsets,
+    values,
+    output,
+    fallback,
+    valid_rows,
+    num_keys,
+    codebook_size: tl.constexpr,
+    logits_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    logits_column_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    prefix_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    prefix_column_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    output_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    child_block: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    first = tl.load(prefixes + row * prefix_row_stride).to(tl.int64)
+    second = tl.load(prefixes + row * prefix_row_stride + prefix_column_stride).to(
+        tl.int64
+    )
+    key = (first * codebook_size + second).to(keys.dtype.element_ty)
+    low = 0
+    high = num_keys
+    while low < high:
+        middle = (low + high) // 2
+        found = tl.load(keys + middle)
+        less = found < key
+        low = tl.where(less, middle + 1, low)
+        high = tl.where(less, high, middle)
+    safe = tl.minimum(low, num_keys - 1)
+    present = (low < num_keys) & (tl.load(keys + safe) == key)
+    start = tl.load(offsets + safe).to(tl.int64)
+    end = tl.load(offsets + safe + 1).to(tl.int64)
+    first_child = tl.load(values + start).to(tl.int64)
+    positions = tl.arange(0, child_block)
+    valid = present & (positions < end - start)
+    children = tl.load(values + start + positions, mask=valid, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    scores = tl.load(
+        logits + row * logits_row_stride + children * logits_column_stride,
+        mask=valid,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    tl.store(output + row * output_row_stride + children, scores, mask=valid)
+    tl.store(fallback + row, first_child)
+    tl.store(valid_rows + row, present)
+
+
+def mask_sparse_prefix_logits(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    prefixes: torch.Tensor,
+    keys: torch.Tensor,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor,
+    values: torch.Tensor,
+    max_children: int,
+    codebook_size: int,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    if (
+        logits.ndim != 2
+        or logits.shape[1] != codebook_size
+        or prefixes.shape != (logits.shape[0], 2)
+        or not keys.numel()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Sparse trie prefixes and logits do not align")
+    output = torch.full_like(logits, -torch.inf, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+    fallback = torch.empty(
+        (logits.shape[0], 1), dtype=torch.int64, device=logits.device
+    )
+    valid_rows = torch.empty(logits.shape[0], dtype=torch.bool, device=logits.device)
+    if logits.shape[0]:
+        _mask_sparse_prefix_logits_kernel[(logits.shape[0],)](
+            logits,
+            prefixes,
+            keys,
+            offsets,
+            values,
+            output,
+            fallback,
+            valid_rows,
+            keys.numel(),
+            codebook_size=codebook_size,
+            logits_row_stride=logits.stride(0),
+            logits_column_stride=logits.stride(1),
+            prefix_row_stride=prefixes.stride(0),
+            prefix_column_stride=prefixes.stride(1),
+            output_row_stride=output.stride(0),
+            child_block=triton.next_power_of_2(max_children),
+            num_warps=8,
+        )
+        torch._assert_async(
+            torch.all(valid_rows), "Trie prefix contains an unknown AB pair"
+        )
+    return output, fallback
+
+
+def materialize_sparse_mask(
+    pair_rows: torch.Tensor,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor,
+    values: torch.Tensor,
+    codebook_size: int,
+    max_children: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    output = torch.zeros(
+        (pair_rows.shape[0], codebook_size),
+        dtype=torch.bool,
+        device=pair_rows.device,
+    )
+    block_size = triton.next_power_of_2(max_children)
+    _materialize_mask_kernel[(pair_rows.shape[0],)](
+        pair_rows,
+        offsets,
+        values,
+        output,
+        output_row_stride=output.stride(0),
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return output
+
+
+def mask_sparse_logits(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    pair_rows: torch.Tensor,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor,
+    values: torch.Tensor,
+    max_children: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    output = torch.full_like(logits, -torch.inf)
+    block_size = triton.next_power_of_2(max_children)
+    _mask_logits_kernel[(pair_rows.shape[0],)](
+        logits,
+        pair_rows,
+        offsets,
+        values,
+        output,
+        logits_row_stride=logits.stride(0),
+        output_row_stride=output.stride(0),
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return output

+        width=width,
+        prefix_width=0 if prefix is None else prefix.shape[1],
+        block=256,

+# Model-native trie beam search
+
+A compatible model bundle may contain `trie_output_head.safetensors`, a
+three-codebook semantic-ID trie. The artifact is static model state, not a
+second learned language-model head. The implementation reuses the original
+LM-head weights.
+
+The artifact contains `root_token_ids`, `level1_token_ids`, `level1_offsets`,
+`level2_token_ids`, and `level2_offsets`, together with the schema metadata
+validated by `trie_config.py` and `trie_constraint.py`.
+
+Full-vocabulary probability normalization is preserved by default.
+`SGLANG_OPT_BEAM_TRIE_TOPK_LOGPROB=true` instead normalizes over retained legal
+candidates. That is an explicit approximation and can change rankings; it must
+not be used to claim full-vocabulary score equivalence.
+
+## Optional fast paths
+
+`SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_ATTENTION=true` enables shared-prompt
+attention for supported FlashInfer MHA FP16/BF16 KV caches. Unsupported
+backend/cache configurations retain ordinary attention. Attention logit caps
+are not supported by the shared-context kernel.
+
+Requests retain their own beam widths. Mixed-width batches use the eager
+width-bucketed shared-context path. Uniform batches can additionally replay
+CUDA graphs when their width and exact row count match the capture configuration:
+
+| Setting | Default | Meaning |
+| --- | ---: | --- |
+| `SGLANG_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_WIDTH` | 2000 | Beam width of graph-compatible groups |
+| `SGLANG_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_GRAPH_MAX_CONTEXT` | 32768 | Context-slot capacity per captured group |
+| `SGLANG_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_GRAPH_MAX_DECODE` | 8 | Private decode-slot capacity per beam |
+
+Configure decode capture buckets to include the exact total beam-row counts
+needed by the workload. A width-1000 workload, for example, needs buckets such
+as 1000, 2000, and 3000 rather than padding a shared-context batch to an
+incompatible row layout. Different per-request decode lengths are supported
+within a uniform-width batch: private slot arrays are padded and actual lengths
+are refreshed for each group on every replay.
+
+`SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_TRIE_SELECTION_GRAPH=true` separately replays the existing
+compact-trie selection tensor operations. It is off by default. Requests with
+other widths, stop-token handling, or unsupported layouts retain the native
+selection path. Every replay restages its inputs and snapshots active tokens,
+parents, scores, and prefixes into request-owned storage.
+
+Normal and speculative decoding retain their ordinary graph keys and capture
+preparation interfaces. Trie graph inputs and output keys are separate, and
+changing a captured scoring/shared-attention configuration rejects stale
+replay. Changing startup-only controls requires restarting or recapturing the
+engine; flags must not be changed to reinterpret an existing graph.
+
+## Correctness and measurement
+
+Verify the original full trie and full-vocabulary score policy independently
+of any compatible synthetic-catalog throughput control. Check ordered
+semantic IDs, sequence scores, membership, uniqueness, output counts, and
+output lengths. Report set overlap or Jaccard similarity separately from
+ordered agreement.
+
+CUDA attention and matrix-multiplication reductions can produce different
+finite-precision trajectories when batch geometry changes. Controlled replay
+equality is not a promise of bitwise equality across arbitrary asynchronous
+batches.
+
+`max_running_requests` is sequence-row capacity, not client concurrency.
+A beam-width-K request uses approximately K decode rows. Report this setting,
+actual graph-path coverage, and whether measured latency includes queueing.

+"""Shared-context decode attention for wide beam batches."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import itertools
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention
+    from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import ScheduleBatch
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.kv.router import KVLayerRouter

+
+class BeamAttentionBucket(msgspec.Struct):
+    row_indices: torch.Tensor
+    context_slots: torch.Tensor
+    context_cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor
+    decode_slots: torch.Tensor
+    beam_width: int
+    decode_lens: torch.Tensor
+
+
+class BeamAttentionMetadata(msgspec.Struct):
+    buckets: list[BeamAttentionBucket]
+    num_rows: int
+
+
+def enabled() -> bool:
+    return envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_ATTENTION.get()
+
+
+def _positive_int(field) -> int:
+    value = field.get()
+    if value <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{field.name} must be positive, got {value}")
+    return value
+
+
+def graph_beam_width() -> int:
+    return _positive_int(envs.SGLANG_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_WIDTH)
+
+
+def graph_max_context() -> int:
+    return _positive_int(envs.SGLANG_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_GRAPH_MAX_CONTEXT)
+
+
+def graph_max_decode() -> int:
+    return _positive_int(envs.SGLANG_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_GRAPH_MAX_DECODE)
+
+
+def supports_shared_context(model_runner) -> bool:
+    from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import AttentionArch
+
+    return (
+        model_runner.decode_attention_backend_str == "flashinfer"
+        and model_runner.sliding_window_size is None
+        and not model_runner.model_config.is_encoder_decoder
+        and model_runner.model_config.attention_arch == AttentionArch.MHA
+        and model_runner.kv_cache_dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
+    )
+
+
+def _metadata_tensor(values, dtype, device):
+    if torch.device(device).type == "cuda":
+        return torch.tensor(values, dtype=dtype, pin_memory=True).to(
+            device, non_blocking=True
+        )
+    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+
+def graph_compatible(metadata, num_rows: int, captured_rows: int) -> bool:
+    if (
+        metadata is None
+        or num_rows != captured_rows
+        or metadata.num_rows != num_rows
+        or len(metadata.buckets) != 1
+    ):
+        return False
+    bucket = metadata.buckets[0]
+    if bucket.row_indices.ndim != 2 or bucket.decode_slots.ndim != 2:
+        return False
+    groups = bucket.row_indices.shape[0]
+    return (
+        bucket.beam_width == graph_beam_width()
+        and bucket.row_indices.shape == (groups, bucket.beam_width)
+        and groups * bucket.beam_width == num_rows
+        and bucket.context_slots.numel() <= groups * graph_max_context()
+        and bucket.context_cu_seqlens.shape == (groups + 1,)
+        and bucket.decode_lens.shape == (groups,)
+        and bucket.decode_slots.shape[0] == groups
+        and bucket.decode_slots.shape[1] <= graph_max_decode() * bucket.beam_width
+    )
+
+
+def build_graph_capture_metadata(num_rows: int, device):
+    width = graph_beam_width()
+    if not enabled() or num_rows < width or num_rows % width:
+        return None
+    groups = num_rows // width
+    rows = [
+        [group]
+        + list(range(groups + group * (width - 1), groups + (group + 1) * (width - 1)))
+        for group in range(groups)
+    ]
+    return BeamAttentionMetadata(
+        num_rows=num_rows,
+        buckets=[
+            BeamAttentionBucket(
+                row_indices=_metadata_tensor(rows, torch.int32, device),
+                context_slots=torch.zeros(
+                    groups * graph_max_context(), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+                ),
+                context_cu_seqlens=torch.arange(
+                    groups + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+                ),
+                decode_slots=torch.zeros(
+                    (groups, width * graph_max_decode()),
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device=device,
+                ),
+                beam_width=width,
+                decode_lens=torch.full(
+                    (groups,), graph_max_decode(), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+                ),
+            )
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def stage_graph_metadata(target, source) -> None:
+    if not graph_compatible(source, source.num_rows, target.num_rows):
+        raise ValueError("Shared-context metadata does not fit the captured graph")
+    if len(target.buckets) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Captured shared-context metadata must have one width")
+    destination, current = target.buckets[0], source.buckets[0]
+    if (
+        destination.beam_width != current.beam_width
+        or destination.row_indices.shape != current.row_indices.shape
+        or current.context_slots.numel() > destination.context_slots.numel()
+        or destination.context_cu_seqlens.shape != current.context_cu_seqlens.shape
+        or destination.decode_lens.shape != current.decode_lens.shape
+        or current.decode_slots.shape[0] != destination.decode_slots.shape[0]
+        or current.decode_slots.shape[1] > destination.decode_slots.shape[1]
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Shared-context metadata exceeds captured buffers")
+    destination.context_slots[current.context_slots.numel() :].zero_()
+    destination.decode_slots[:, current.decode_slots.shape[1] :].zero_()
+    destination.row_indices.copy_(current.row_indices)
+    destination.context_slots[: current.context_slots.numel()].copy_(
+        current.context_slots
+    )
+    destination.context_cu_seqlens.copy_(current.context_cu_seqlens)
+    destination.decode_slots[:, : current.decode_slots.shape[1]].copy_(
+        current.decode_slots
+    )
+    destination.decode_lens.copy_(current.decode_lens)
+
+
+def build_metadata(
+    batch: ScheduleBatch,
+    model_runner: ModelRunner,
+) -> Optional[BeamAttentionMetadata]:
+    if batch.beam_tail is None or not batch.forward_mode.is_decode() or not enabled():
+        return None
+    if not supports_shared_context(model_runner):
+        return None
+    entries = batch.beam_tail.entries
+    if not entries or batch.seq_lens_cpu is None:
+        return None
+
+    widths = [entry.end - entry.start + 1 for entry in entries]
+    if any(width <= 1 for width in widths):
+        return None
+    if sum(widths) != len(batch.seq_lens):
+        return None
+
+    num_base_rows = batch.beam_tail.num_base_rows
+    req_to_token = model_runner.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token
+    entries_by_width: dict[int, list] = {}
+    for entry, beam_width in zip(entries, widths, strict=True):
+        entries_by_width.setdefault(beam_width, []).append(entry)
+
+    buckets = []
+    for beam_width, bucket_entries in entries_by_width.items():
+        group_rows = _metadata_tensor(
+            [
+                [entry.leader_idx]
+                + list(
+                    range(
+                        num_base_rows + entry.start,
+                        num_base_rows + entry.end,
+                    )
+                )
+                for entry in bucket_entries
+            ],
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device=batch.device,
+        )
+        req_rows = batch.req_pool_indices[group_rows]
+
+        context_parts = []
+        decode_parts = []
+        prompt_lens = []
+        decode_lens = []
+        for group_index, entry in enumerate(bucket_entries):
+            prompt_len = int(entry.group.prompt_len)
+            seq_len = int(batch.seq_lens_cpu[entry.leader_idx])
+            decode_len = seq_len - prompt_len
+            if decode_len <= 0:
+                return None
+            group_req_rows = req_rows[group_index]
+            context_parts.append(
+                req_to_token[group_req_rows[:1], :prompt_len].reshape(-1)
+            )
+            decode_parts.append(
+                req_to_token[
+                    group_req_rows,
+                    prompt_len:seq_len,
+                ]
+                .transpose(0, 1)
+                .reshape(-1)
+            )
+            prompt_lens.append(prompt_len)
+            decode_lens.append(decode_len)
+
+        max_decode_len = max(decode_lens)
+        padded_decode_parts = []
+        for decode_part in decode_parts:
+            padding = max_decode_len * beam_width - decode_part.numel()
+            if padding:
+                decode_part = torch.cat(
+                    [
+                        decode_part,
+                        torch.zeros(
+                            padding,
+                            dtype=decode_part.dtype,
+                            device=decode_part.device,
+                        ),
+                    ]
+                )
+            padded_decode_parts.append(decode_part)
+
+        buckets.append(
+            BeamAttentionBucket(
+                row_indices=group_rows.to(dtype=torch.int32),
+                context_slots=torch.cat(context_parts),
+                context_cu_seqlens=_metadata_tensor(
+                    [0, *itertools.accumulate(prompt_lens)],
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device=batch.device,
+                ),
+                decode_slots=torch.stack(padded_decode_parts),
+                beam_width=beam_width,
+                decode_lens=_metadata_tensor(
+                    decode_lens,
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device=batch.device,
+                ),
+            )
+        )
+
+    return BeamAttentionMetadata(buckets=buckets, num_rows=len(batch.seq_lens))
+
+
+def forward(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    layer: RadixAttention,
+    forward_batch: ForwardBatch,
+    kv_layers: KVLayerRouter,
+) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    metadata = forward_batch.beam_attention_metadata
+    if metadata is None:
+        return None
+    if layer.logit_cap > 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Shared-context beam attention does not support attention logit caps; "
+            "disable SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_ATTENTION for this model."
+        )
+
+    k_buffer, v_buffer = kv_layers.read(layer.layer_id).kv()
+    if k_buffer.ndim != 3 or v_buffer.ndim != 3:
+        raise RuntimeError("Shared-context attention requires 3D MHA K/V cache buffers")
+
+    q_heads = layer.tp_q_head_num
+    head_dim = layer.head_dim
+    flat_q = q.contiguous().view(metadata.num_rows, q_heads, head_dim)
+    output = torch.empty_like(flat_q)
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.beam_shared_context import (
+        shared_context_attention,
+    )
+
+    for bucket in metadata.buckets:
+        shared_context_attention(
+            flat_q,
+            k_buffer,
+            v_buffer,
+            bucket.row_indices,
+            bucket.context_slots,
+            bucket.context_cu_seqlens,
+            bucket.decode_slots,
+            bucket.decode_lens,
+            output=output,
+            softmax_scale=layer.scaling,
+        )
+    return output.view(-1, q_heads * head_dim)

+
+A model opts in with ``"beam_trie_output_head": true`` in config.json and ships
+``trie_output_head.safetensors`` at its root. Metadata (integer strings):
+``format_version`` = 1, ``token_start``, ``codebook_size``, ``num_codebooks`` = 3;
+the SID token for depth ``d`` and code ``c`` is
+``token_start + d * codebook_size + c``. Tensors are 1-D integer CSR arrays of
+codes relative to their codebook: sorted unique ``root_token_ids``; per root,
+``level1_offsets`` into sorted unique ``level1_token_ids``; per level-1 entry,
+``level2_offsets`` into sorted ``level2_token_ids``. Offsets start at 0, end at
+the child-array length, and no group is empty.
+"""

+
+import functools
+import logging
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+from safetensors import safe_open
+from transformers import PretrainedConfig
+from transformers.utils import cached_file
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_FILENAME = "trie_output_head.safetensors"
+# config.json key a model sets to true to bundle the trie output head.
+TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_CONFIG_KEY = "beam_trie_output_head"
+TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_FORMAT_VERSION = 1
+
+
+class TrieOutputHeadConfig(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    tensor_path: str
+    token_start: int
+    codebook_size: int
+    num_codebooks: int
+
+    @property
+    def token_end(self) -> int:
+        return self.token_start + self.num_codebooks * self.codebook_size
+
+    def token_start_for_depth(self, depth: int) -> int:
+        if not 0 <= depth < self.num_codebooks:
+            raise ValueError(f"SID depth {depth} is outside [0, {self.num_codebooks})")
+        return self.token_start + depth * self.codebook_size
+
+
+def _metadata_int(metadata: dict[str, str], name: str) -> int:
+    try:
+        return int(metadata[name])
+    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_FILENAME} metadata requires integer {name!r}"
+        ) from exc
+
+
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)
+def load_trie_output_head_config(tensor_path: str) -> TrieOutputHeadConfig:
+    path = Path(tensor_path).expanduser()
+    if not path.is_file():
+        raise ValueError(f"Trie output-head tensors do not exist: {path}")
+    path = path.absolute()
+
+    with safe_open(path, framework="pt", device="cpu") as tensors:
+        metadata = tensors.metadata() or {}
+
+    format_version = _metadata_int(metadata, "format_version")
+    if format_version != TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_FORMAT_VERSION:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Unsupported trie output-head format version: "
+            f"{format_version}; expected {TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_FORMAT_VERSION}"
+        )
+    token_start = _metadata_int(metadata, "token_start")
+    codebook_size = _metadata_int(metadata, "codebook_size")
+    num_codebooks = _metadata_int(metadata, "num_codebooks")
+    if token_start < 0 or codebook_size <= 0 or num_codebooks != 3:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Trie output head requires a non-negative token_start, "
+            "a positive codebook_size, and exactly three codebooks"
+        )
+
+    return TrieOutputHeadConfig(
+        tensor_path=str(path),
+        token_start=token_start,
+        codebook_size=codebook_size,
+        num_codebooks=num_codebooks,
+    )
+
+
+def discover_trie_output_head_config(
+    hf_config: PretrainedConfig,
+    model_path: str,
+    vocab_size: int,
+    revision: Optional[str] = None,
+    *,
+    is_draft_model: bool,
+) -> Optional[TrieOutputHeadConfig]:
+    # The trie head belongs to the target model; a draft model never loads it.
+    if is_draft_model or not getattr(hf_config, TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_CONFIG_KEY, False):
+        return None
+    # A model that opts in must ship the artifact; a missing file raises.
+    tensor_path = cached_file(model_path, TRIE_OUTPUT_HEAD_FILENAME, revision=revision)

+    if config.token_end > vocab_size:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "The model-bundled beam trie SID token range exceeds the "
+            f"model vocabulary: end={config.token_end}, "
+            f"vocab_size={vocab_size}"
+        )
+    logger.info("Discovered model-native trie output head at %s", config.tensor_path)
+    return config

+    def _sparse_level2_rows(self, prefix_codes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sparse = self.level2_sparse
+        assert sparse is not None
+        size = self.config.codebook_size

+        safe_rows = pair_rows.clamp_max(sparse.keys.numel() - 1)
+        valid = ~(
+            (pair_rows == sparse.keys.numel()) | (sparse.keys[safe_rows] != ab_rows)
+        )
+        if pair_rows.is_cuda:
+            torch._assert_async(
+                torch.all(valid),
+                "Trie prefix contains an unknown AB pair",
+            )
+        elif not torch.all(valid):
+            raise ValueError("Trie prefix contains an unknown AB pair")
+        return pair_rows

+    def _sparse_level2_mask(self, prefix_codes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sparse = self.level2_sparse
+        assert sparse is not None
+        size = self.config.codebook_size
+        pair_rows = self._sparse_level2_rows(prefix_codes)
+        if pair_rows.is_cuda:
+            from sglang.kernels.ops.grammar.trie_mask import materialize_sparse_mask

+            return materialize_sparse_mask(
+                pair_rows,
+                sparse.offsets,

+                self.config.codebook_size,
+                sparse.max_children,
+            )
+        starts = sparse.offsets[pair_rows].long()
+        lengths = sparse.offsets[pair_rows + 1].long() - starts
+        total_values = int(lengths.sum().item())
+        mask = torch.zeros(
+            (prefix_codes.shape[0], size),
+            dtype=torch.bool,
+            device=prefix_codes.device,
+        )
+        if total_values == 0:
+            return mask
+        output_rows = torch.repeat_interleave(
+            torch.arange(prefix_codes.shape[0], device=prefix_codes.device),
+            lengths,
+            output_size=total_values,
+        )
+        range_bases = torch.cumsum(lengths, dim=0) - lengths
+        value_indices = torch.arange(
+            total_values,
+            device=prefix_codes.device,
+        ) + torch.repeat_interleave(
+            starts - range_bases,
+            lengths,
+            output_size=total_values,
+        )
+        child_codes = sparse.values[value_indices].long()
+        mask[output_rows, child_codes] = True

+    def valid_child_mask(self, prefix_codes: torch.Tensor, depth: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        size = self.config.codebook_size
+        if depth == 0:
+            if prefix_codes.shape != (1, 0):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Depth-zero prefix state must have shape (1, 0), got "
+                    f"{tuple(prefix_codes.shape)}"
+                )
+            return self.root_mask.unsqueeze(0)
+        if prefix_codes.ndim != 2 or prefix_codes.shape[1] != depth:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Expected prefix state [rows, {depth}], got "
+                f"{tuple(prefix_codes.shape)}"
+            )
+        if depth == 1:
+            return self.level1_masks[prefix_codes[:, 0]]
+        if depth == 2:
+            rows = prefix_codes[:, 0] * size + prefix_codes[:, 1]
+            if self.level2_masks is not None:
+                return self.level2_masks[rows]
+            return self._sparse_level2_mask(prefix_codes)
+        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported SID depth: {depth}")
+
+    def topk_logprobs(
+        self,
+        pieces: Sequence[torch.Tensor],
+        prefix_codes: torch.Tensor,
+        depth: int,
+        num_candidates: int,
+        normalizers: Optional[Sequence[torch.Tensor]] = None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Score valid children from dense or compact normalized logits.
+
+        Dense logits preserve the full-vocabulary score exactly: normalize over the
+        full vocabulary, then gather valid SID tokens. Compact logits use a
+        streamed full-vocabulary normalizer supplied by the output head.
+        """
+
+        sparse_cuda = (
+            depth == 2
+            and self.level2_sparse is not None
+            and pieces
+            and pieces[0].is_cuda
+            and all(piece.shape[1] == self.config.codebook_size for piece in pieces)
+        )
+        masks = None if sparse_cuda else self.valid_child_mask(prefix_codes, depth)
+        token_start = self.config.token_start_for_depth(depth)
+        size = self.config.codebook_size
+        vals, toks = [], []
+        row_start = 0
+        if normalizers is not None and len(normalizers) != len(pieces):
+            raise ValueError("Beam trie logits and normalizer pieces must align")
+        for piece_index, piece in enumerate(pieces):
+            rows = piece.shape[0]
+            if rows == 0:
+                continue
+            row_masks = None if masks is None else masks[row_start : row_start + rows]
+            row_start += rows
+            x = piece.float()
+            if x.shape[1] == size:
+                if normalizers is None:
+                    from sglang.srt.beam_search.trie_output_head import (
+                        use_topk_logprob,
+                    )
+
+                    if not use_topk_logprob():
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            "Compact beam trie logits require full-vocabulary "
+                            "normalizer metadata"
+                        )
+                else:
+                    normalizer = normalizers[piece_index]
+                    if normalizer.shape != (rows, 2):
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            "Beam trie normalizer rows must match compact logits"
+                        )
+                codebook_logits = x
+            else:
+                token_end = token_start + size
+                if x.shape[1] < token_end:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"Dense beam logits width {x.shape[1]} does not cover "
+                        f"SID token range [{token_start}, {token_end})"
+                    )
+                codebook_logits = x[:, token_start:token_end]
+            if sparse_cuda:
+                candidates, fallback = self._mask_sparse_level2_logits(
+                    codebook_logits,
+                    prefix_codes[row_start - rows : row_start],
+                )
+            else:
+                candidates = codebook_logits.masked_fill(
+                    ~row_masks,
+                    -torch.inf,
+                )
+                fallback = row_masks.to(torch.int64).argmax(
+                    dim=-1,
+                    keepdim=True,
+                )
+            k = min(num_candidates, size)
+            v, t = torch.topk(candidates, k, dim=-1)
+            # Wide beams can retain score-dead (-inf) candidates. Keep their
+            # token IDs on-trie so a later decode never indexes an empty prefix.
+            t = torch.where(torch.isneginf(v), fallback, t)
+            if x.shape[1] == size:
+                if normalizers is None:
+                    vals.append(v - torch.logsumexp(v, dim=-1, keepdim=True))
+                else:
+                    vals.append(
+                        (v - normalizer[:, :1].float()) - normalizer[:, 1:].float()
+                    )
+            else:
+                vals.append(v - torch.logsumexp(x, dim=-1, keepdim=True))
+            toks.append(t + token_start)
+        if row_start != prefix_codes.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Beam logits rows ({row_start}) do not match trie prefix rows "
+                f"({prefix_codes.shape[0]})"
+            )
+        values, tokens = torch.cat(vals), torch.cat(toks)
+        if depth == 0 and values.shape[1] < num_candidates:
+            padding = num_candidates - values.shape[1]
+            values = torch.cat(
+                [
+                    values,
+                    torch.full(
+                        (values.shape[0], padding),
+                        -torch.inf,
+                        dtype=values.dtype,
+                        device=values.device,
+                    ),
+                ],
+                dim=1,
+            )
+            tokens = torch.cat(
+                [tokens, tokens[:, :1].expand(-1, padding)],
+                dim=1,
+            )
+        return values, tokens
+
+    def advance_prefixes(
+        self,
+        prefix_codes: torch.Tensor,
+        parent_idx: torch.Tensor,
+        next_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+        depth: int,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        token_start = self.config.token_start_for_depth(depth)
+        codes = next_tokens - token_start
+        return torch.cat([prefix_codes[parent_idx], codes.unsqueeze(1)], dim=1)

+
+        output = shared_context_attention(

+            context_cu_seqlens,
+            decode_slots,

+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.codebook_projection import project_active_codebook_logits
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci

+    not (
+        torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] == 9
+        and hasattr(torch, "_grouped_mm")
+    ),
+    reason="SM90 grouped GEMM required",
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [1024, 8193])
+def test_active_codebook_projection_is_exact_and_graph_safe(num_rows):
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    hidden_size, codebook_size = 128, 256
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(
+        (num_rows, hidden_size), device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    weights = torch.randn(
+        (3 * codebook_size, hidden_size),
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    )
+    depths = torch.arange(num_rows, device=device) % 3
+
+    project_active_codebook_logits(hidden_states, weights, depths, codebook_size)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        actual = project_active_codebook_logits(
+            hidden_states, weights, depths, codebook_size
+        )
+
+    for next_depths in (depths.clone(), torch.ones_like(depths)):
+        depths.copy_(next_depths)
+        graph.replay()
+        all_logits = torch.matmul(hidden_states, weights.T).view(
+            num_rows, 3, codebook_size
+        )
+        expected = all_logits[torch.arange(num_rows, device=device), next_depths]
+        assert actual is not None
+        assert torch.equal(actual, expected)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import sys
+
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

issue_comments.body:
Pushed fixes for:

- **KV reservation on every beam request**: only fixed-length trie groups now report an exact decode budget (`BeamGroup.decode_slot_budget()`), and the existing admission estimates use it without extra state; ordinary beam search keeps main's estimate. Priority preemption still skips beam groups, since `release_req` does not free a group's member rows (9934b0fe90).
- **FlashInfer hook on every decode layer**: shared-context attention is now `BeamSharedContextFlashInferAttnBackend`, a FlashInfer subclass selected only when `SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_ATTENTION` is set; `flashinfer_backend.py` is back to main. The workspace resize is dropped, since it only served 20k-row trie decode graphs (59fe6636e6).
- **Beam branches inside `_get_logits`**: `_get_logits` is back to main; `forward()` calls `_get_beam_trie_logits` for compact-trie rows (22f3d4b7cb).
- **Trie decode graph variant**: trie and shared-context batches run eagerly, which removes the capture kwargs shim and the extra `ShapeKey` field (0e91bff157).
- **Hub lookup on every model start**: the trie head loads only when `config.json` sets `"beam_trie_output_head": true`, through `cached_file`; a declared but missing artifact now fails startup instead of silently dropping the constraint (2e20e9605a).
- `BeamCoordinator` loads the trie itself, so `scheduler.py` is back to main (455831aa74).
- The trie and shared-context forward-batch fields are built in the beam modules; `ForwardBatch.init_new` makes two calls (6a3b3886bf).
- The Triton kernels move to `sglang.kernels.ops` (`attention.beam_shared_context`, `gemm.codebook_projection`, `grammar.trie_mask`) with their tests (881da8d2a5).

Verified on one H200 with a synthetic Qwen3-0.6B + 3x8192 SID model and a 1M-item trie, beam width 1000 and 2000: ordered beams match the previous head at concurrency 1 in eager, graph, shared-context, and mixed-width runs; the differences at concurrency 4-10 are within the previous head's own run-to-run variance; ordinary beam search matches main. Throughput is equal or higher, and peak memory is about 20 GB lower in graph mode.

Model bundles need `"beam_trie_output_head": true` in `config.json`.

### Full original LiHA: +7.2% completed QPS versus the previous PR head

Baseline is this OSS PR's previous head, `b2d120e596d1226012ba29daa6f588038e26ad07`. The update is `45b352b`; its final Git tree is identical to the measured implementation, before splitting that implementation into seven feature-sized commits.

Original full trie and unchanged model weights, with full-vocabulary projection/normalization. One H200, BF16 weights/KV, beam width 1,000, 1,000 three-token SIDs per request, and prefix cache disabled. Two fresh-process runs per version, each with 50 warmups and 1,000 measured requests. Offered load was 54 QPS using Poisson arrivals with no client-concurrency limit. Latency includes queueing through the complete response.

| Implementation | Mean completed QPS | Completed QPS, run 1 / 2 | p95 latency, run 1 / 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous PR head `b2d120e` | 49.70 | 49.756 / 49.635 | 2.059 / 2.514 s |
| This update `45b352b` | **53.28** | **52.776 / 53.789** | **0.976 / 1.272 s** |

All 4,000 measured responses had the requested count and length, with no invalid or duplicate SIDs. The controlled 1,000-request full-trie correctness replay produced **1,000/1,000 identical ordered SID lists**, **maximum sequence-score difference 0**, **mean/minimum Jaccard 1.0**, and **mean/minimum beam overlap 1,000/1,000**. Ordinary greedy output checks and mixed ordinary/beam compatibility probes passed. Controlled equality does not imply bitwise equality across arbitrary asynchronous batch geometries.

Runtime used the v0.5.21 dependency line: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18, SGLang kernel 0.4.7.0+cu130, Transformers 5.12.1, Tokenizers 0.22.2, and CUDA Tile 1.6.0rc5. The current head's newer minimum-version startup guard was explicitly disabled for this compatibility run; dependency declarations were unchanged. Both versions used an isolated `beam_trie_output_head=true` config, unchanged weights/trie bytes, 32,032 sequence rows, memory fraction 0.30, MessagePack IPC, post-warmup GC freeze, configured GC thresholds, and delayed sampling disabled.

The baseline implementation always runs beam batches eagerly; its unused dense-graph capture capacity was reduced to 1,000 rows to avoid startup OOM without changing that serving path. This update captured exact 1,000-32,000-row trie graph buckets. These are measurements at the stated offered load, not estimates of globally maximal throughput. All earlier runs, including the earlier tail-latency outlier, were retained; this table reports the complete fresh rerun rather than selecting individual repetitions.
